samples.summary: resolveRelsTarget still has no root containment: excess `..` segments silently escape the package root
samples.evidence: The change adds a root-relative branch but leaves the normalization loop unguarded: `if (seg === '..') stack.pop();` (rels.ts:58) pops an already-empty stack without error, so `resolveRelsTarget('ppt/slides/slide1.xml', '../../../../../../etc/passwd')` returns `etc/passwd` and `resolveRelsTarget(p, '/../../x')` returns `x`. An attacker crafts a .pptx whose slide rels Target walks above the package root. Today that is NOT exploitable: every consumer I traced (image.ts:78→archive.readBytes, chart.ts:258, slide.ts:158,222, index.ts:261,326,350,390) passes the result only to `zip.file(path)` in unzip.ts:40/43, which is an in-memory lookup over a fully attacker-supplied archive — no filesystem or network sink exists in packages/slides/src. The exposure is that this is an exported, general-looking path resolver whose doc comment now advertises package-root semantics; a future consumer that joins the result onto a real base directory (the CLI already has `writeFileSync` in packages/cli/src/slides/content.ts:58) turns it into classic zip-slip. Clamping (drop `..` when the stack is empty) costs one condition and removes the class.
searchedFor: grep for fetch(|readFile|from 'fs|node:fs|path.join|createReadStream under packages/slides/src (no matches)
grep resolveRelsTarget across the repo and read every call site
read packages/slides/src/import/pptx/unzip.ts for the archive sink
read packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-import.ts and content.ts for filesystem sinks
grep startsWith('ppt/ for any path allowlist that the leading slash could bypass (no matches)

samples.summary: Attacker-controlled file extension reaches a prototype-chain lookup on EXT_TO_MIME, yielding a non-string MIME that flows into Blob type / data: URL
samples.evidence: `const ext = mediaPath.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase() ?? ''; const mime = EXT_TO_MIME[ext] ?? 'application/octet-stream';` (image.ts:85-86). `mediaPath` is the resolveRelsTarget output — fully attacker-controlled via the rel Target and zip entry name. `EXT_TO_MIME` is a plain object literal, so a media part named `.../image1.__proto__` makes `EXT_TO_MIME['__proto__']` return `Object.prototype` (truthy, so `??` does not fire) and `.constructor` returns `Function`. That non-string value is passed as `mime` to `uploadImage`, where the frontend does `new Blob([bytes], { type: mime })` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pptx-actions.ts:37) and the CLI interpolates it into a `data:${mediaType};base64,...` URL (packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-import.ts:23). I could not turn this into a concrete XSS or content-type confusion — the reachable values stringify to `[object Object]` / `function Object() { [native code] }`, which browsers reject as MIME rather than honor — so this is unsafe input handling, not a confirmed exploit. Pre-existing line, not added by this diff, but it sits directly downstream of the resolver the diff widens. A `Map` or an `Object.create(null)` table removes it.

samples.summary: Root-relative targets add a new alias family to a de-dupe keyed on the RAW rel target, widening duplicate-import work amplification
samples.evidence: `orderedMasterTargets` de-dupes on the unresolved string (`seen.has(rel.target)`, index.ts:287/294) while `loadMasterAndLayouts` resolves it later (index.ts:350). Before this change a `<p:sldMasterId>` entry spelled `/ppt/slideMasters/slideMaster1.xml` failed to resolve and bailed cheaply at the `if (!masterXml)` guard (index.ts:352); after it, the alias resolves and the same master plus all its layouts are re-imported, and every master/layout `blipFill` background is re-uploaded through `uploadImage` (image.ts:90) once per alias. An attacker ships a tiny deck whose `<p:sldMasterIdLst>` lists one master under many distinct raw spellings (`/ppt/...`, `./ppt/...`, `ppt/./...`, arbitrarily deep) to multiply image uploads against the workspace /images endpoint from a few hundred bytes of XML. Amplification is linear, and equivalent relative aliases already worked pre-change, so this is a marginal widening of a pre-existing vector rather than a new one — the change's own lessons doc records the de-dupe inconsistency as a known limitation. De-duping on the resolved path (as `orderedSlidePaths` at index.ts:261 already does) closes it.
searchedFor: traced loadMasterAndLayouts image upload path into image.ts parseBlipFill

samples.summary: isSafeHref passes scheme-less and protocol-relative external rel targets on the stated rationale that they 'resolve under the host's own origin'
samples.evidence: `if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:/i.test(target)) return true;` (text.ts:575) accepts any target without a scheme, including `//evil.com/phish`, which is protocol-relative and resolves off-origin — contradicting the comment at text.ts:573-574. It also accepts same-origin paths like `/workspaces/x/delete?...`, turning an untrusted imported deck into a same-origin clickable link. Impact is near zero in practice because `https://evil.com` is already allowed by the same allowlist (text.ts:577), so protocol-relative adds no new reach; the finding is that the guard's stated reasoning is wrong, not that it is bypassable in a way that matters. Pre-existing and untouched by this diff; reported only because it is in the rels/target handling this change lives in.
